report.summary: Converted 9 reviewed findings into 7 delivery items: 3 high-severity (kill-switch, digest collision, uncheckable side-effects), 3 medium (evidence propagation, harvest lossless, digest inconsistency, eval isolation), 1 low (tokenizer label).
risks: Adding a test for kill-switch may reveal that the fix requires a new registration mechanism, increasing effort.
Digest collision fix may require changing the digest length or adding a salt, which could break existing stored selections.
Uncheckable side-effects may require significant refactoring to make eval/picker side-effect-free.
Evidence placeholder handling may require changes in multiple downstream consumers.
Harvest lossless change may alter existing behavior; need to ensure no regression.
Digest consistency fix may require changing TaskSpec.body generation; could affect serialization.
Egress docstring fix is low risk but may expose deeper inconsistency.
Eval isolation test may fail if current imports violate the rule; need to clean up imports.
Tokenizer label fix is simple but may miss heuristic tokenizers if naming convention is not consistent.
todos: Confirm that _register exception handling is the only way processes are tracked.
Decide on digest length increase (e.g., 128 bits) and migration strategy.
Audit eval/correctness.py and picker.py for side-effects.
Identify all downstream consumers of evidence.text/content.
Determine if harvest should merge purposes or keep existing behavior.
Verify TaskSpec.body generation for optional fields.
Check egress docstring for trusted lane behavior.
Ensure eval does not import structcore internals.
Verify tokenizer names in drift.py for heuristic substring.

items.title: Fix unregistered process kill-switch by ensuring registration always succeeds or alternative kill mechanism exists
items.why_now: Without this fix, a process that fails registration cannot be killed, causing resource leaks and potential system hang.

steps.do: In daedalus/core/process.py, modify _register to never raise an exception; log the failure and register the process anyway, or use a fallback kill mechanism (e.g., process group ID).
steps.verified_by: Write test that forces exception in _register (mock side effect) and verify process is still killable via _LIVE or alternative.

items.assumption: The only way to kill a process is through _LIVE dictionary.

items.title: Increase digest length in Selection to at least 128 bits to avoid collisions
items.why_now: Current 64-bit digest has high collision probability at scale, leading to incorrect selection identification.

steps.do: In daedalus/core/selection.py, change digest computation to use 32 hex characters (128 bits) of SHA256 instead of 16.
steps.verified_by: Run test that creates two different selections and asserts digests differ; verify birthday bound test passes.

items.assumption: No external system depends on the exact digest length.

items.title: Audit and fix uncheckable side-effects in eval and picker code
items.why_now: Claims of no side-effects in eval/correctness.py and picker.py are unverifiable; side-effects could cause data corruption or inconsistent state.

steps.do: Inspect full implementations of _run_lists, worktree creation, docrefs.scan, and write_snapshot in eval/correctness.py and picker.py; ensure no file writes, vendor calls, or state mutations. Add explicit assertions or logging to verify.
steps.verified_by: Run tests that mock filesystem and verify no writes occur; add unit tests for each function.

steps.do: In daedalus/eval/picker.py, similarly audit and test for side-effects.

items.assumption: The full source of these files is available for audit.

items.title: Ensure downstream consumers of Evidence check for placeholder text
items.why_now: If downstream code treats placeholder text as actual content, it may silently process unreadable files, leading to incorrect results.

steps.do: Search for usage of evidence.text or evidence.content in council/ and kairos/; add checks for placeholder patterns (e.g., 'UNREADABLE') and handle appropriately (e.g., skip or raise).
steps.verified_by: Write test that provides Evidence with placeholder text and asserts downstream consumer raises error or skips.

items.assumption: Placeholder patterns are consistent across the codebase.

items.title: Fix harvest function to merge purposes instead of skipping when key exists and name unknown
items.why_now: Current behavior may lose information if a new purpose differs from existing one for an unknown env name.

steps.do: In daedalus/core/harvest.py, modify the condition to add purpose even if key exists but name is unknown; merge purposes (e.g., append to list or set).
steps.verified_by: Write test that calls harvest with existing key and new purpose; verify both purposes are stored.

items.assumption: Merging purposes does not break downstream expectations.

items.title: Ensure digest consistency by always including all optional fields in TaskSpec.body
items.why_now: If optional fields are conditionally omitted, semantically equivalent specs can have different digests, causing false mismatches.

steps.do: In daedalus/core/taskspec.py lines 561-586, verify all optional fields are always set (e.g., to None) in the dict; if not, add defaults.
steps.verified_by: Write test that creates two TaskSpecs with same required fields but different optional fields omitted; assert digests are equal.

items.title: Add import guard to prevent eval from importing structcore internals
items.why_now: No enforcement of isolation promise; future changes could accidentally couple eval to structcore.

steps.do: Add a test in daedalus/eval/__init__.py or a new test file that verifies no structcore internals are imported: grep -rn 'import.*structcore' daedalus/eval/
steps.verified_by: Run the test; it should pass (no imports).

items.assumption: No structcore imports currently exist in eval.

items.title: Fix tokenizer label fragility by using explicit mapping instead of substring check
items.why_now: Renaming a tokenizer could silently break the label logic.

steps.do: In daedalus/core/slice.py, replace substring 'heuristic' check with an explicit list of heuristic tokenizer names or a flag.
steps.verified_by: Write test that uses a tokenizer with 'heuristic' in name but not heuristic; assert label is correct.

items.assumption: Tokenizer names are defined in drift.py and can be enumerated.
